t: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array II
o: Index i is beautiful if s[i..i+|a|−1] = a and some occurrence j of b satisfies |j−i| <= k. With |s| up to 5e5, naive matching is too slow. Compute all occurrence lists of a and b with the Z-algorithm (linear time), then for each occurrence i of a, binary-search the sorted b-occurrence list for any j in [i−k, i+k].
k: Z-algorithm finds all pattern occurrences in O(|s| + |pattern|).
Sorted occurrence lists + binary search answers the '|j−i| <= k' proximity query in O(log n) per a-occurrence.
Concatenation trick: run Z on pattern + '#' + text; positions with z-value = |pattern| are exact matches.

a.i: Build z-array of a+'#'+s and b+'#'+s to extract occurrence indices A and B (B is naturally sorted). For each i in A, bisect B for the first j >= i−k; if it exists and j <= i+k, i is beautiful.
s: Extract occurrence starts of a and b in s.
For each a-occurrence i, binary search B in [i−k, i+k]; emit i on success.
a.t: O(|s| + |a| + |b| + m log m) — Z-computation is linear; each of the m a-occurrences does one binary search.

w: Alternatives: KMP failure functions or rolling hashes (watch collisions; double hashing or verify matches). A two-pointer merge of A and B also answers proximity in O(m + p) without binary search. Pitfalls: separator '#' must not occur in inputs (lowercase guaranteed); remember occurrence offsets subtract (pattern length + 1). Follow-up: streaming text, or k varying per query.
